title: 1936 Prairie: the Allerton house stands as itself
items: The Thompson/Allerton villa at Prairie and 20th, the grandest house in the 1869 South Division, replaces the district's placeholder block: two tall storeys of red pressed brick over a brownstone basement, a deep bracketed cornice, a low hipped roof with a railed deck, and the belvedere tower rising past the cornice, built to the sizes the Chicago Tribune printed in October 1869 and the 1911 fire map's plan.

Its columned verandah with the balcony on top, the reception room's half-octagonal bay toward 20th Street, the library's canted bay on the north and the kitchen range behind are all there, and the old winter photograph of the house now has a camera you can compare it against.
